sn12.23:1.1: Near Sāvatthī … the Exalted One said:
sn12.23:1.2: “In him who knows, Monks, who sees do I say that the intoxicants are extinct, not in him who knows not, neither sees.
sn12.23:1.3: And in what, Monks, in him who knows, in him who sees are the intoxicants extinct?
sn12.23:1.4: Thus is material shape, thus is its uprising, thus its passing away.
sn12.23:1.8: thus is consciousness, thus is their uprising, thus their passing away.
sn12.23:1.9: Now in extinction, the knowledge about extinction:
sn12.23:2.1: that I say is causally associated, not the opposite.
sn12.23:2.2: And what is that which is the cause of knowledge about extinction?
sn12.23:2.4: I say that liberation is causally associated, not uncausally associated.
sn12.23:2.5: And what is that which is the cause of liberation?
sn12.23:2.7: I say that passionlessness is causally associated with liberation.
sn12.23:2.8: And what is that which is the cause of passionlessness?
sn12.23:2.10: I say that repulsion is causally associated with passionlessness.
sn12.23:2.11: And what is that which is the cause of repulsion?
sn12.23:2.12: The knowledge and the vision of things as they really are is the answer.
sn12.23:2.13: I say that the knowledge-and-vision of things as they really are is causally associated with repulsion.
sn12.23:2.14: And what is that which is the cause of the knowledge and insight of things as they really are?
sn12.23:2.16: I say that concentration is causally associated with the knowledge and vision of things as they really are.
sn12.23:3.1: And what is that which is the cause of concentration?
sn12.23:3.3: I say that happiness is causally associated with concentration.
sn12.23:3.4: And what is that which is the cause of happiness?
sn12.23:3.6: I say that serenity is causally associated with happiness.
sn12.23:3.7: And what is the cause of serenity?
sn12.23:3.9: I say that rapture is causally associated with serenity.
sn12.23:3.10: And what is the cause of rapture?
sn12.23:3.12: I say that joy is causally associated with rapture.
sn12.23:3.13: And what is the cause of joy?
sn12.23:3.15: I say that faith is causally associated with joy.
sn12.23:4.1: And what is the cause of faith?
sn12.23:4.3: I say that suffering is causally associated with faith.
sn12.23:4.4: And what is the cause of suffering?
sn12.23:4.6: I say that birth is causally associated with suffering.
sn12.23:4.8: so also is becoming with birth.
sn12.23:6.1: Now therefore, Monks, activities are in causal association with ignorance,
sn12.23:6.2: consciousness is in causal association with activities,
sn12.23:6.18: the knowledge and vision into things as they really are with concentration,
sn12.23:6.19: repulsion with the knowledge and vision into things as they really are,
sn12.23:6.22: knowledge about extinction [of intoxicants] with liberation.
sn12.23:7.1: Just as when, Monks, on some hilltop when rain is falling in thick drops, that water, coursing, according to the slope, fills the hillside clefts and chasms and gullies, these being filled up fill the tarns, these being filled up fill the lakes, these being filled up fill the little rivers, these being filled up fill the great rivers, and the great rivers being filled up fill the sea, the ocean—
sn12.23:8.1: even so, Monks, there is causal association of activities with ignorance, of consciousness with activities, of name-and-shape with consciousness, of the sixfold sense-sphere with name-and-shape, of contact with the sixfold sense-sphere, of feeling with contact, of craving with feeling, of grasping with craving, of [renewed] becoming with grasping, of birth with [renewed] becoming, of sorrow with birth, of faith with sorrow, of joy with faith, of rapture with joy, of serenity with rapture, of happiness with serenity, of concentration with happiness, of the knowledge and vision of things as they really are with concentration, of repulsion with the knowledge and vision of things as they really are, of passionlessness with repulsion, of liberation with passionlessness, of knowledge about extinction [of intoxicants] with liberation.”
